prompt_en:
Create a low seated environmental portrait inside a traveling theatre prop vault during a controlled blackout. One clearly adult person sits immediately behind the artifact. The attached portrait guides only this visible adult appearance: long dark wavy hair, brown eyes, a neutral expression, a black blouse, and a small gold necklace. The adult balances the mounted photograph on a small conservation easel and turns a hinged raking-light panel toward its surface. Dust motes cross a single emergency lantern beam among stacked painted scenery, open specimen drawers, rope coils, and faded stage flats. Use a low seated portrait with the artifact on a small easel in the near foreground and the adult immediately behind it; keep the adult face readable and the entire card contained within the frame.

The artifact depicts a portable darkroom beside an archaeological trench. Build it as a thin photographic paper sheet visibly attached to a distinctly thicker cream card mount. It is thin photographic paper attached to thicker card, with the thin sheet visibly bonded to a distinctly thicker cream card mount. Give the image a smooth or semi-gloss albumen surface, revealed by a narrow grazing highlight confined to the photographic layer. Preserve fine image detail, with tiny excavation tools, canvas folds, numbered stakes, glass bottles, and distant workers remaining crisp. The complete print-to-card boundary is visible on all four sides. An oblique edge clearly reveals the thin image sheet above the thicker matte mount, so the two layers remain readable even at thumbnail scale. Show overall fine crackle or microscopic paper fiber visible through the albumen layer, minute and continuous across the whole image. Keep that texture hair-fine, evenly distributed, and subordinate to the trench imagery.

A pencil-thin warm raking beam skims diagonally across the mounted print while a dim cool emergency-lantern fill retains natural detail in the adult face and the depth of the prop vault. The specular sweep ends precisely at the photographic-paper edge; the cream card perimeter stays softly diffuse and matte. Render a convincing contemporary editorial photograph with tactile paper depth, coherent hands and easel geometry, natural skin texture, and enough resolved detail for native-scale inspection.

authorial_decisions.rationale: The two-level light makes gloss, matte card, microtexture, portrait appearance, and setting simultaneously inspectable without changing any locked dimension.

decisions.rationale: Full-body emphasis would shrink the mounted print below reliable material-review scale.
A magazine medium would substitute a publication surface for the frozen physical historical photograph.
Clean digital texture would suppress the required process-linked albumen microtexture.
Generic window light lacks the narrow grazing highlight needed to bound gloss to the image layer.
Even overcast diffusion would flatten the print-card thickness difference and surface reflectance.
Golden-hour backlight conflicts with the controlled blackout and conservation raking-light event.
